label: AFFECTION

cover.headline: 5 ways to say *“I miss you”* without starting a fight

points.heading: Lead with a good memory
points.body: Start from something you both enjoyed. It tells him what you want more of.
points.panel: “I was thinking about our Saturday mornings. I loved those.”

points.heading: Say “I miss,” not “you never”
points.body: Both come from the same feeling. Only one of them invites him closer.

points.heading: Make it small and soon
points.body: A vague wish is easy to agree with and easy to forget. Name a time.
points.panel: “Could we take a walk after dinner tomorrow?”

points.heading: Own your part of the drift
points.body: Distance usually has two authors. Saying so lowers the guard on both sides.
points.panel: “I know I’ve been buried in work, too.”

points.heading: Let it be an invitation
points.body: He may not match your words right away. Leave the door open instead of keeping score.
points.panel: “No pressure. I just wanted you to know.”

close.save: Save this for when you’re missing him.

caption:
“I miss you” and “You’re never here” come from exactly the same place. One sounds like an invitation. The other sounds like a charge.

If you’re missing him, say that part. Here are five ways to put it so it sounds like what it is.
